hints: Recall the first law of thermodynamics $\Delta U = q + w$, where $w$ is work done on the gas and $q$ is thermal energy supplied.
For constant volume path $P \to Q$, work done is zero, so the increase in internal energy equals the heat supplied.

Use the fact that over the complete cyclic process $P \to Q \to R \to P$, the net change in internal energy must be zero.
Determine $\Delta U$ for path $R \to P$, and use $\Delta U = q + w$ to find the heat supplied during $R \to P$.
